question.problem:
$$

$$

Consider the vector $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ By evaluating the following quadratic forms at $x$ **only,** determine which of them **cannot** be negative-definite.

I. $R(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}$

II. $S(x)={x}^{T}\,[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]x$

III. $T(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$
question.worked_solution:
A quadratic form $Q(x)$ is negative-definite if $Q(x)<0$ for all $x\in {R}^{n}∖\{0\}.$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the quadratic forms by substituting $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]:$

- Quadratic form I *cannot* be negative-definite since 

$$
\begin{aligned}R(x) & ={5}^{2}+2(0)^{2} \\  & =25+0 \\  & =25>0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Quadratic form II *might* be negative-definite. Indeed,

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-50<0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Quadratic form III *cannot* be negative-definite since

$$
\begin{aligned}T(x) & ={5}^{2}-{0}^{2}+2\cdot 5\cdot 0 \\  & =25+0 \\  & =25>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
